subject: Day 67: track sleep windows
bodyText:
Today's focus
With the wind-down routine in place, today is about reading Avi's wake-window patterns. At 6 to 12 weeks most infants tolerate 60-to-90-minute wake windows across four to five naps; logging a few days reveals his.

Action items
- Log every wake window and nap length for the next two to three days; by 12 to 14 weeks the pattern firms up enough to anchor a loose schedule rather than guessing at tired cues. AAP HealthyChildren: baby sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Protect the first nap of the day, which is usually the easiest to install and sets the rhythm for the rest of the day. AAP HealthyChildren: baby sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- If he skips a nap, bank the lost sleep at the next sleep period with an earlier bedtime by 30 to 60 minutes rather than a late-afternoon makeup nap.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Variable nap quality day to day, and 30-to-45-minute catnaps; both are typical at 2 to 4 months and age out around 5 to 6 months.
- [monitor] Asymmetric movement or a persistent head-turn to one side; raise it at the next visit if repositioning does not resolve it.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting unrelated to any recent vaccine, or a clear drop in wet-diaper output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 if his lips look blue!

Enrichment opportunities
- Keep the sleep log running for a few days; the wake-window pattern stabilizes by 12 to 14 weeks and is what lets you anchor a loose daily schedule. AAP HealthyChildren: baby sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Vary the tummy-time surface (firm mat, your lap, a slight incline) and keep a toy just out of reach to drive scooting and stretching effort. AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Play the Suzuki Book 1 recording during a calm awake window; pre-instrument listening exposure can begin now at no cost and primes the mother-tongue listening approach. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; the log you build now feeds directly into it.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
- Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression typically begins; baseline data on his current windows will make the shift easier to read.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
